title: Evaluating Effectiveness of Enforcement on Pedestrian-only Paths and Cycling Lanes
what_it_is: Evaluating Effectiveness of Enforcement on Pedestrian-only Paths and Cycling Lanes

sections.label: Cycling paths and enforcement
sections.summary: Dedicated cycling paths are red and two metres wide, with shared paths, safety measures and enforcement of the POP rule.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Dedicated cycling paths are distinctly coated in red with a width of two metres, sufficient for two cyclists to pass.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Where space is a constraint, shared paths are used.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This allows both cyclists and pedestrians to share the path, typically at a width of 2.5 metres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: To enhance pedestrian safety, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) works with relevant agencies to implement additional safety measures, such as installation of convex mirrors at locations with line-of-sight issues, additional lighting and trimming of overgrown hedges that narrow the paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Since August 2024, LTA’s active mobility enforcement officers have been on the ground to educate users on the safe use of the segregated paths, ahead of the commencement of the POP rule on 1 July 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA conducts more checks at hotspots with frequent instances of errant riding behaviour, based on feedback received.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Warnings and subsequently, fines are given to those who intentionally disobey the rule, especially those who endanger others with errant riding behaviour.

sections.label: Fines and accident assistance
sections.summary: About five fines have been issued since 1 July 2025, and riders must stop and render assistance after accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In fact, since 1 July 2025, about five fines have been issued for such errant riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: On the recourse, under the Active Mobility Act, when accidents happen, the cyclist or rider are supposed to stop and render assistance.
